pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered a strongly positive reaction and tied it directly to his own experience: 'I love that. I realize I didn't explicitly mention the mobility aspect, but yeah, that's very important to me. That's what I perceive to be a shortcoming from every single program that I've purchased, including my current one.' He went on to say he feels ignorant on mobility and is looking forward to learning it. This is the clearest pillar-to-goal connection in the batch.

The stronger reaction had come earlier and unprompted during discovery: 'I appreciate that approach, because it's actually revolutionary, right, like all the other coaches, their business model is to, you know, keep working with you forever, right... and I resist that.'

anchors.raw: I'm wrapping up a one-year-long program with this other coach that is like rather famous on Instagram, not as famous as Trevor
anchors.competitor: an Instagram coach, name garbled in the transcript
anchors.note: Not a price anchor but a risk anchor, and it is what produced the objection. He paid this coach up front for a year and got a qualified result - 'I wouldn't say that I don't see the return in the investment at all, because I do see some things, but it's not exactly what I thought it was going to be.' That experience is the reason he would not pay $6,000 up front and the reason a trial period had to be invented.

anchors.raw: I invested in this one-year-long program, and so I did pay upfront, and it's not like I regret it, but, you know, it's been one year.
anchors.note: The other side of the same anchor and the more useful one commercially: he has paid a full year up front for online coaching before, and has bought several three- and six-month Instagram programmes over the years. He is an established buyer of exactly this category at meaningful prices.

anchors.raw: all the other coaches, their business model is to, you know, keep working with you forever, right, to like sculpt you, and I resist that, like, I think, you know, one can learn everything there is to learn, about one's body
anchors.note: He actively prefers a finite, teach-and-release model over an indefinite subscription, which is the exact shape of the six-month offer. This is the strongest supporting anchor on the call and the rep used it well.

anchors.raw: I commute to go to the gym, I mean, it's not far, it's, like, 25 minutes each way, but, like, I have to do that, because that's the gym that I have found, that doesn't get crazy crowded
anchors.note: Roughly fifty minutes of commuting per session in a city where gyms are overcrowded, plus programmes that require machines his gym does not stock. The minimal-equipment, train-anywhere proposition has real monetary value to him and he raised it himself.

unmet_demand.want: To experience the programme before committing the full amount - 'I require some proof points in experience, to then commit the full, not only the money, but also my effort'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no trial, no pilot and no guarantee in the offer. The rep had to invent a $1,200 one-month walk-away period on the call to satisfy it, which means the demand is real, recurring and currently met only by improvisation.

unmet_demand.want: 10-15 lb of additional muscle with broader shoulders, a bigger chest and developed hamstrings - his primary stated physical goal
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Whether kettlebell-based full-body training delivers hypertrophy for a lean 42-year-old who has already plateaued at 3,000 calories was never substantiated. The rep reframed the physique goal as a by-product of mobility and longevity and the prospect accepted the reframe, but the original demand was not answered and the same question surfaced independently on another call in this batch.

unmet_demand.want: Continued use of a gym and heavy loading alongside the programme, since he has just spent a year building the habit and does not want to abandon it
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partly answered - the rep said he could train at the gym or at home - but nothing addressed how kettlebell programming coexists with or replaces the heavy resistance work he has been doing four to five times a week.
